definition: A chemical change caused by passing an electric current through a compound which is either molten or in solution.
msAccepts: chemical change/decomposition caused by passing electricity through a molten or dissolved compound
splitting a substance by electricity
msAvoids: any heating effect of a current (metals warm but no chemical change)
a physical change such as melting

definition: A liquid or solution that undergoes electrolysis. Electrolytes contain ions, whose movement carries the current and causes the chemical changes.
msAccepts: a liquid/solution containing ions that conducts and is decomposed by electricity
msAvoids: any conducting solid (metals conduct by electrons)
a substance that conducts without undergoing chemical change

definition: A conductor, usually carbon (graphite) or platinum, that carries the electric current into and out of the electrolyte.
msAccepts: carbon/graphite or platinum rods dipping into the electrolyte
conductors through which current enters/leaves the electrolyte

definition: An electrode that does not react chemically during the electrolysis, such as carbon (graphite) or platinum.
msAccepts: an electrode that does not react/take part in the reaction
unreactive electrode (carbon, platinum)
msAvoids: any metal electrode (reactive metals like copper do take part)

definition: The positive electrode in electrolysis. Anions are attracted to it, and oxidation (loss of electrons) happens there.
msAccepts: positive electrode
electrode where anions go / oxidation occurs
msAvoids: the negative electrode (that is the cathode)
confusing the sign with the electron flow direction

definition: The negative electrode in electrolysis. Cations are attracted to it, and reduction (gain of electrons) happens there.
msAccepts: negative electrode
electrode where cations go / reduction occurs
msAvoids: the positive electrode (that is the anode)

definition: A negatively charged ion, named because it is attracted to the anode (the positive electrode).
msAccepts: negative ion
ion attracted to the anode/positive electrode
msAvoids: a positive ion (that is a cation)
any negative particle such as an electron

definition: A positively charged ion, named because it is attracted to the cathode (the negative electrode).
msAccepts: positive ion
ion attracted to the cathode/negative electrode
msAvoids: a negative ion (that is an anion)

definition: An ionic equation showing the reaction at one electrode only — either oxidation or reduction — with electrons written as e⁻ on one side.
msAccepts: equation for one electrode showing electron gain or loss
ionic equation with electrons on one side
msAvoids: a full molecular equation with electrons on both sides

definition: The removal of an ion from the electrolyte at an electrode, by giving up or taking electrons, so that it becomes a neutral atom.
msAccepts: ion loses/gains electrons at an electrode and becomes an atom/molecule
ion converted to a neutral species at an electrode

definition: The loss of electrons. Oxidation always happens at the anode during electrolysis. Memory aid: OILRIG.
msAccepts: loss of electrons
gain of oxygen (historical use)
msAvoids: anything to do with oxygen exclusively

definition: The gain of electrons. Reduction always happens at the cathode during electrolysis. Memory aid: OILRIG.
msAccepts: gain of electrons
loss of oxygen (historical use)

definition: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen at the same time — one species loses electrons as another gains them.
msAccepts: oxidation and reduction occurring together
electron transfer between two species

definition: Water, which ionises only very slightly into hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions, which constantly recombine (a reversible process).
msAccepts: water ionises slightly/reversibly to H⁺ and OH⁻
only a small fraction of water molecules are ionised
msAvoids: water contains no ions at all

definition: The list of metals (with carbon and hydrogen) ordered by reactivity. It decides which ions are discharged in solution electrolysis.
msAccepts: a ranked list of reactivity used to predict displacement/discharge
order of metals from most to least reactive
msAvoids: a list with no predictive use

definition: A substance, such as sugar, that contains no ions when molten or in solution, so it neither conducts electricity nor undergoes electrolysis.
msAccepts: a substance that does not conduct or decompose because it has no ions
msAvoids: a substance that conducts but does not change

definition: An outer-shell electron no longer attached to any particular atom or bond, free to move throughout the metallic structure and carry the current.
msAccepts: electrons free to move through the whole metal
not attached to any particular atom
msAvoids: free electrons (as a definition — name them delocalised)

definition: A regular arrangement of particles repeated in three dimensions. In an ionic lattice the ions are held in fixed positions and cannot move.
msAccepts: regular/repeating arrangement of ions
giant three-dimensional structure of particles
